faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week (usually 38 for full-time) and then by 52 weeks. For example, $30 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $59,280 per year. This assumes no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% on top of the base hourly rate, compensating for the lack of paid leave. For the National Minimum Wage, casual employees receive $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25). Always check if your rate already includes casual loading before using a calculator.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated and is it included in my salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your salary at 12% of ordinary earnings (from 1 July 2026), up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. It is not part of your take-home pay; your employer pays it separately into your super fund.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Hourly Rates to Annual Pay: A Complete Guide

Whether you’re negotiating a job offer, comparing roles, or planning your budget, knowing how to convert an hourly rate to an annual salary is essential. This guide uses the latest official figures from the Fair Work Commission and the Australian Taxation Office, and references the **Hays Salary Guide 2026 PDF** to give you context on typical market rates. Remember, the most reliable sources are government agencies, not recruiter surveys.

### The Basic Formula

The standard calculation for annual gross pay is:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

For full-time employees in Australia, the typical working week is 38 hours (as defined by the National Employment Standards). If you work a different number of hours, adjust accordingly. The formula assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

For example, if your hourly rate is $30.00:
- Weekly pay: $30.00 × 38 = $1,140.00
- Fortnightly pay: $1,140.00 × 2 = $2,280.00
- Annual gross: $1,140.00 × 52 = $59,280.00

You can use [the timesheet](/) on this site to do the calculation instantly. Just enter your base hourly rate and check the casual loading box if applicable.

### National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. This is the minimum for award/agreement-free employees. Most workers are covered by an award, which sets higher minimum rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) with the exact rates for each award, including allowances and penalty rates.

Award wages increased by 4.75% from 1 July 2026. Always check the specific award that applies to your job.

### Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave (annual leave, sick leave). For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25). When using a calculator, never add casual loading to a rate that already includes it. Our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how to handle this correctly.

### Superannuation Is Paid on Top

Superannuation is not part of your salary; it’s an additional payment your employer makes into your super fund. From 1 July 2026, the Super Guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For example, if your annual salary is $80,000, your employer must contribute $9,600 in super (12% of $80,000). This stops once your earnings exceed the cap. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more details.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your annual gross salary is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office uses a progressive tax scale for residents in 2026–27:
- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus, the Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income (with reductions for low-income earners). Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator to estimate your net pay after tax and Medicare.

### Using the Hays Salary Guide 2026 PDF

The **Hays Salary Guide 2026 PDF** is a popular resource for salary benchmarks across industries. It surveys over 12,000 respondents and provides typical salary ranges for many roles. However, remember that this is a recruiter survey, not an official source. Always cross-check with award rates from the Fair Work Ombudsman and data from the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS).

For example, the Hays guide may show a typical salary of $100,000 for a marketing manager, but the award minimum might be lower. The ABS Average Weekly Earnings (May 2026) for full-time adult ordinary time employees is $2,083.70 per week, or about $108,352 annually. For all employees (including part-time), average total earnings are $1,579.20 per week, or $82,118 annually.

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross, simply multiply your weekly pay by 2. For the National Minimum Wage:
- Weekly: $1,004.90
- Fortnightly: $2,009.80

If you’re paid monthly, multiply weekly by 4.33 (or annual divided by 12). Our [reference tables](/data) include conversion factors for different pay periods.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay calculated here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For personalised advice, consult a qualified accountant or use the ATO’s tax estimator.

### Summary

- Use the formula: hourly × hours per week × 52 for annual gross.
- The standard full-time week is 38 hours.
- The National Minimum Wage is $26.44/hour (2026–27).
- Casual loading adds 25% on top.
- Super is 12% paid by your employer, not from your salary.
- The **Hays Salary Guide 2026 PDF** provides market benchmarks but verify with official sources.
- Use our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) and [average pay](/topics/average-pay) pages for more data.
